beats.say: You hear the distant clang of battle drums as Ranjit Singh's forces storm Lahore in 1799, defying expectations.
Most recall his empire's glory, but few know the secret treaty with the British that saved his navy.
beats.visual: British East India Company treaty document 1809

beats.say: In 1809, the East India Company supplied six cannons, demanding a tiny trade concession at Amritsar.
Ranjit's vizier, Fakir Azizuddin, turned the pact into a diplomatic shield, keeping French ambitions at bay.
While the world feared a Sikh naval threat, the hidden fleet quietly patrolled the Indus, deterring rebels.
In 1813, the British withdrew a planned invasion, fearing the empire's unexpected artillery range.
That same year, Ranjit ordered the construction of the formidable Ramgarh fort, a stone wall unseen by Europeans.
The fort's hidden cannon pits could fire 300 meters, outmatching the British field guns at the time.
When Ranjit died in 1839, the treaty dissolved, and the British seized the fleet, erasing the secret.
History whispers that without that covert armament, the Sikh Empire might have crumbled much sooner.
